title: Exact target matching leaves axon preservation effects uncertain in selected Allen mouse and human slice pairs
abstract: We tested whether the positive link between intact source axons and detected connections remains after exact target matching. We used Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1 small and matched source class, Cre label, layer and 100 micrometre distance bins. The mouse sample had 253 pairs from 45 inferred animals. Its intact minus truncated connection rate was +4.63 percentage points, with a nominal 97.5% donor bootstrap interval of -1.04 to 10.67 points. The human sample had 50 pairs from six inferred donors. Its contrast was +5.07 points, with interval -3.14 to 19.63. Only 12 mouse and four human detected connections support these estimates. Most eligible pairs lacked matched support. A mouse broad-class sensitivity interval was positive, but the richer primary match and narrower bins did not resolve an effect. These results do not refute the earlier recording-matched finding. They show that exact target control leaves large uncertainty. Qualitative labels, sparse overlap, inferred donors and response detection effects prevent a causal loss estimate or transfer claim. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and external evidence regeneration steps are supplied. External records are not bundled.

display.caption: Exact target matched connection rate contrasts. Bars are nominal 97.5% inferred-donor bootstrap intervals. Sensitivity rows are descriptive. The mouse broad-class match is positive, but primary intervals include zero in both species.
